newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- UTILITIES LOBBY GROUP BACKED BY HESELTINE

Deputy prime minister Michael Heseltine is to lead a Commons attack on Labour's plans for a 'windfall tax' on privatised utilities by endorsing proposals for a lobby group comprising all the privatized companies. The formation of the group has been suggested by leading industrialists, who see it as a vehicle for presenting a united front to promote the benefits of privatisation. Separately, Labour's windfall tax plans also face attack from US energy groups with UK interests.
-- GRANADA EXPECTED TO MOVE TOWARDS DEMERGER IN 1997

Media and leisure group Granada is reported to be favouring proposals for a demerger of its television interests from its hotel and catering operations. Hints that a restructuring, possibly as early as mid-1997, is likely emerged as Granada reported a 37 percent increase in annual pre-tax profits to 480m sterling.
-- EUROPEAN FUTURES RIVALS LINK UP WITH CHICAGO

Both the London futures and options exchange (LIFFE) and its French counterpart Matif have announced link-ups with a US market, the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. The moves come as European centres jockey for supremacy in the run-up to economic and monetary union (Emu). Chicago is the world centre for derivatives trading, and the European exchanges hope that linking up with the CME will ensure their survival after the introduction of a single currency in Europe.
-- CLARKE BUOYED BY SURGE IN GROWTH OF RETAIL SALES

Figures from the Office for National Statistics reveal that retail sales in October rose at the fastest rate for two years. Retail sales volumes surged by a seasonally adjusted 4 percent in the three months to October compared to the same period in 1995, with the biggest increases in large food stores. However, the release of the figures coincided with statistics showing the fastest growth since January of the quantity of money in circulation, adding to pressure on chancellor Kenneth Clarke to raise interest rates.
-- ROLLS-ROYCE IN MOVE FOR SNECMA AERO ENGINE LINK

British aerospace and engineering group Rolls-Royce has extended an invitation to French counterpart Snecma to take part in the development of its Trent 900 engine. Rolls-Royce sees the Trent 900 as the engine for the future generation of 550-seat aircraft. A possible sticking point to any co-operation agreement is Snecma's long-term alliance with Rolls' US rivals General Electric.
-- CAR INDUSTRY RECORDS BEST EVER OCTOBER

Figures released by the Office for National Statistics reveal that car production in the UK in October soared to its highest-ever level for that month. The figures show an increase of 39.3 percent in October car output in 1996, compared to 1995, to a total of 179,963 units. Industry body the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders described the figures as the clearest evidence yet of a solidly-based resurgence for the UK car sector.
-- CHIROSCIENCE IN $120m BIOTECH DEAL

Cambridge-based biotechnology company Chiroscience is to acquire a US-based counterpart, Darwin Molecular, in a takeover deal worth $120m (72m stg). Bill Gates, the billionaire founder of computer software giant Microsoft, has a 14 percent stake in Seattle-based Darwin, and he will take a 3 percent stake in Chiroscience as part of the deal. Agreement for the deal, which will increase the number of drugs Chiroscience has in development, has been reached after a year of talks.
-- C&W IN TALKS WITH NYNEX ON CABLE LINK DEAL

British-based telecommunications group Cable & Wireless, which reported a 9 percent increase in interim profits on Wednesday, is reported to be in discussions with US telecoms giant Nynex over a possible alliance. The proposed deal would involve Nynex, a regional operator in the US, taking a stake in C&W's planned $500m transatlantic cable link. In return, C&W would gain greater access to international traffic generated by companies based in the region around New York, the home base of Nynex.
-- MIDLAND STEPS CLOSER TO ETHNIC BANK DEAL

Midland Bank, a member of the HSBC financial group, is reported to be in advanced negotiations with a group of UK-based Asian businessmen over the launch of a new bank. Midland is expected to take a 45 percent stake in the new venture, with the group of 20 businessmen likely to hold 6 percent. The balance of the equity would be held by outside investors, with the promoters of the venture keen to attract Asian shareholders.
-- RIO POWER GROUP STAKE SOLD

An international consortium which includes Spain's Endesa, Electricidada de Portugal, and Chilectra of Chile has acquired a 70.2 percent stake in the Brazilian electricity distribution company Cerj for R$605m (US$587m). Cerj, which has 4,400 employees and 1.2m customers, made losses of R$62m last year. The winning consortium group is led by Chilectra, which is stumping up R$360m for the deal, with EdP contributing R$182m and Endesa R$60.5m.
